title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
Problem VI: an elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) has both ends A and B free and is held by a pin ('stylus') at an interior point C. It may rotate about C but cannot be displaced there. The task is to find its free vibration modes.

Euler first sets out the matching conditions at C in physical terms.
- The deflection vanishes at C for all time.
- The lamina cannot form a finite angle anywhere, so the angles ACE and BCF made by the two portions with the axis must be equal. This is continuity of slope across the support. With x measured from A and x' from B, the slopes are equal and opposite in the local coordinates.
- Because both angles vanish together and reach their maxima together, both portions must oscillate with the same period. The separation parameter θ is therefore common to both segments; this is a single global eigenfrequency.
- The pin nevertheless produces a 'saltus in lege continuitatis': the part CF moves differently from how it would without the pin. In modern terms the pin reaction makes the shear force (the third derivative) jump at C, while deflection, slope and (as the next page uses) moment stay continuous.

Notation: AC = α, BC = β, α + β = a. Coordinates are x from A on one side and x' from B on the other, with Φ = θx/b and Φ' = θx'/b. The general separated solution of b^4 y'''' = −θ^4 y·(time factor) on each segment is
  y = cos(θθt)(A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{−Φ}),
and similarly with primes on the other segment. The bracket closes on the next page.

The next page carries the setup forward:
- free-end conditions y'' = y''' = 0 at each end;
- y = 0 at C from each side, written with ζ = θα/b and ζ' = θβ/b;
- six equations for eight constants, to be closed by matching slope and curvature at C.
The result is a transcendental frequency equation in ζ and ζ' with ζ/ζ' = α/β. This is the classical free–free beam with an intermediate pinned support.
errors: No substantive error on this page. The equal-angle argument correctly gives slope continuity, and the remark that the pin produces a discontinuity correctly corresponds to a jump in shear force (y''') at the support.
The displayed formula for y lacks its closing parenthesis; this is a typographical slip in the print. The bracket closes in the analogous formula for y' on the next page.

ideas.what: Interface conditions at an intermediate pinned support: zero deflection, continuous slope and moment, and a jump in shear caused by the reaction.
ideas.modern_name: Continuity/jump conditions for multi-span Euler–Bernoulli beams (transfer conditions at a simple intermediate support)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443, 1773); later systematised in Clebsch, Rayleigh and Navier-type multi-span beam theory
ideas.where_published: E443 (Novi Commentarii 17); discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: A common frequency parameter θ on both segments: the eigenvalue problem is global, not segment-wise.
ideas.modern_name: Global eigenfrequency of a piecewise-defined (coupled) Sturm–Liouville-type fourth-order problem

ideas.what: Separated solution with cos, sin, e^Φ and e^{−Φ} on each segment.
ideas.modern_name: Standard beam mode shape basis (trig/hyperbolic functions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a set-up page for the intermediate-support problem in E443. The paper and its treatment of supported laminae are covered in Truesdell's historical commentary. The physical reasoning about the continuity 'saltus' is nice, but it is known and standard.
transcription_corrections: The formula 'y=cos.θθt(A cos.Φ+B sin.Φ+Ce^Φ+De^{-Φ}' lacks its closing parenthesis in the print itself; this is not an OCR error.
'vocetur pro priori parte' is likely 'vocetur' as printed (sense: 'vocetur ... AX = x'). The transcription otherwise matches the image.
